newsitem.title: UK: Centrica posted 452 mln stg '96 9-month loss.
newsitem.headline: Centrica posted 452 mln stg '96 9-month loss.

text.p: Centrica, the gas supply business which will be spun off from British Gas in February, posted a pre-tax loss of 452 million stg over the first nine months of 1996, Centrica said on Friday in its listings document.
The loss was mainly due to the absence of one of the year's two winter quarters, Centrica said.
It posted a 1995 pre-tax profit of 307 million stg, compared with a 366 million stg profit in 1994 and a 259 million loss in 1993, when it incurred a 910 million stg restructuring charge.
The company, which will also includes the Morecambe Bay gas field, confirmed analysts' expectations by saying it did not anticipate to pay dividends in the immediate future.
Centrica said its prospects mainly hinge on its performance in the domestic gas market, which is in the process of being opened up to competition.
Centrica did not say which market share it expected to hold in the domestic market. But it added its share in the market for big industrial and commercial customers continued to fall.
Centrica added that its prospects will also be influenced materially by the market price of gas compared with the price it has to pay under the long-term take-or-pay contracts.
These deals, signed mostly before privatisation in 1986, oblige it to buy fixed amounts of gas from North Sea producers even if it cannot find a market.
Centrica, which re-negotiated three contracts, estimates that the future cost of committed contracts is 26 billion pounds.
Centrica gave no clues on any progress of renegotiations of more take-or-pay contracts.

British Gas shareholders have to approve the demerger at a meeting on February 12. It is expected that trading in Centrica shares will begin on February 17 if shareholders approve the formation of Centrica.

The demerger was first announced in February 1996. It is aimed to separate the loss-making supply business, which will cease to be regulated in due course, from the profitable transportation operations, which will remain regulated by industry watchdog Ofgas.
Shareholders will receive one Centrica share for each British Gas share.
Centrica said its pro forma balance sheet per September 30, 1996, showed net assets of 2.887 billion stg.
In a recent report, brokers Merrill Lynch said they value Centrica at 1.775 billion stg or 40 pence per share.
